newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Branson prepares for around world balloon flight. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Branson prepares for around world balloon flight. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]

text.p: British tycoon Richard Branson started his final preparations on Monday at a Marrakesh airbase in Morocco for his record beating round-the-world balloon trip.
"The weather is the best in this season. We will leave Marrakesh at between 6.30 a.m. and 7.30 a.m. on Tuesday, we will get to the Himalayas in India in the first five-day leg," Branson said.
Marrakesh has been chosen as the ideal launch pad for sending the ballon into the winds as it is on the faster, southerly sub-tropical jet stream.

Branson said the flight will cross over Algeria, Libya Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, Hong Kong, Japan, across the Pacific, America and the Atlantic before landing in England.
"No matter how long the trip will take to go round the world ...the main thing is to be the first person to do it," Branson told Reuters.
The flight was estimated to take between 14 and 21 days, with a "realistic" time seen of about 18 days.
"I am feeling confident and enjoying that the day has come for the trip. We've got superb weather. We will be away tomorrow as we've got a fantastic weather forecast," Branson added.
He said the total operation would cost sponsors between 1.5 ($2.5 million) and two million pounds.
Branson, the 46-year-old-boss (corrects age from 45) of Virgin group of companies, was thwarted last January by constant bad weather from making the attempt.
A group of 40 technicians worked from dawn to fix telecommunication gear aboard the white-coloured balloon capsule on the Marrakesh military airfield.
"The technicians will start inflating the balloon for nearly 12 hours from 06.00 p.m," a company spokeswoman said.
Branson's co-pilots Per Linstrand and Rory McCarthy, a hang-gliding champion, were with the flamboyant tycoon.

The three-man team spent three days training in the new balloon in December and have been waiting since then for ideal weather in Morocco to take them straight into the southerly sub-tropical jet stream.

The balloon flight is the latest in a series of record-breaking attempts that have indulged Branson's taste for adventure while earning publicity for his businesses ranging from Virgin Atlantic Airways to contraceptives.
